evals.prompt: Document the credit pricing and overage charges feature of the fixture
evals.expected_output: be-feature-documenter (via /dev:document-feature) writes a three-level set under docs/features/ of a git-committed copy of evals/fixture/: <feature>.md, <feature>.behind-the-scenes.md, <feature>.technical.md, matching the golden examples in shape, with every fact traced from the fixture rather than taken from the goldens.
expectations: The three level files for the feature exist under docs/features/: the guide <name>.md, <name>.behind-the-scenes.md and <name>.technical.md; the only other files for it there are Level 3 topic splits named <name>.technical.<topic>.md
`python3 scripts/doc-lint.py --dir <output dir>` exits 0
The exact values £6.00, 8 credits, 24 hours and 3 credits appear in the Level 1 guide

The Level 1 worked example contains at least one overage arithmetic line of the form shortfall credits × rate = amount, built only from values that exist in the fixture (tier costs 1/2/3, plan allowances 8 or 16 credits, rates £6.00 or £5.00, or a personal rate the example states as an assumption), and every arithmetic line in the example is correct
No `#confirmed` tier tag appears in any of the three level files except the one sentence in Level 3's `How to read this` legend that says it is never written

Level 1 contains no HTTP status code, no file name (*.cs, *.json), no class name (e.g. CreditPricingService, BookingCancelledHandler, OverageChargeJob, Outbox) and neither the word 'handler' nor 'outbox'

Level 3 has a Finding that a redelivered booking confirmation is priced twice (no idempotency key), with a boundary condition (e.g. delivery fails after the save, the retry spends credits / accrues overage a second time)

Levels 1 and 2 contain none of the words bug, defect, flaw, broken, wrong, mistake, vulnerability or 'should have'; where they mention double pricing on redelivery they state it as behaviour without judging it (Level 2 may state at-least-once delivery neutrally)
Level 3 reports that no telemetry exists beyond a single start-up log line (Telemetry section states the search that found nothing)
Level 1 uses the client terms 'Session credits', 'Overage' and 'Monthly allowance'
Level 1 quotes the exact refusal text "That plan name is already taken"
Level 2 names the parts by plain role names (no class names) and Level 3 maps each of those role names to its class/file
All three level files carry the same commit sha in their stamp line, and each carries an Audience line (Level 1 shareable, Levels 2 and 3 internal)

Golden-copy check: Level 2 or Level 3 states that a failed cancellation return is retried like booking pricing (3 attempts in total, then set aside/parked); no level says returns are never retried or have no failure path
Golden-copy check: Level 2 or Level 3 states that waiting confirmations and cancellations are picked up every 5 seconds; no level says the delay is unknown or not visible from the code
Golden-copy check: no level says staff (or anyone) can configure or change session tiers or their credit costs
Golden-copy check: no level says staff (or anyone) can set or clear a member's personal overage rate through the system

Golden-copy check: no level says a crash part-way through monthly posting leaves some members charged and others not; if Level 3 discusses a partial failure of monthly posting, it is that allowances can be reset while no charges are saved

Golden-copy check: every file path cited in Level 3 exists in the fixture (e.g. src/Workshops.Api/Credits/CreditPricingService.cs); none of src/Credits/…, src/Shared/Outbox.cs or migrations/007 appears
Golden-copy check: at least one level names a second plan, Plus, with 16 credits a month at £5.00 per overage credit

Scope, split and sessions are confirmed: two areas, one session each, in this order - plans and credits (plan settings, the member's credits page, booking pricing, cancellation returns, monthly overage posting), then bookings and sessions (booking a seat, cancelling a booking, cancelling a session). evals.expected_output: be-documenter (via /dev:document-system) surveys a git-committed copy of evals/fixture/, and because the confirmed reading plan holds two sessions it writes one runnable plan under docs/plans/ in the library's plan format and stops without tracing or documenting any area.
expectations: Exactly one plan exists, at docs/plans/NNN-document-<system>.md with a zero-padded NNN; its title line is `# NNN — <title> — plan (YYYY-MM-DD)` followed by a **Goal:** line and a **Status:** line that says the split is confirmed, nothing is documented yet and which task is next
Nothing was documented in the survey session: docs/business-model/areas/ holds no area file and no system-overview file exists

`## 1. What already exists, and what is missing` is a `| Need | Today | Gap |` table with one row per area whose Today cell cites fixture paths with line numbers, plus rows for the system overview and the shared KB files

A numbered section holds the confirmed area map with AREA ids, and every surface of the fixture is in exactly one area or the parked list: the five HTTP routes mapped in Program.cs, the monthly overage job, and the two message handlers with the outbox that delivers to them

The tasks are A1, A2 and K1 in that order, each with `**Stack:** `docs` · **Agent:** `be-documenter``, exactly one **Deliverable:** stated as a result, a **Depends on:** line, a **Budget:** with itemized drivers that follow 85,000 + traced source lines × 12 + 25,000, and a **Gate** line
A2 depends on A1 and K1 depends on A1 and A2; no task is said to run beside another, and a decision records why (the shared KB files and the reading order)
Every task's gate runs doc-lint.py over docs/business-model; A1 and A2 use the `Gate: own tests` form and K1 the last-runnable-task form
The plan says it writes no code and therefore has no acceptance tests, coverage floor or telemetry smoke
`## Close-out — every task` is present directly above the prompts with all eight steps of the plan format's close-out

`## Prompts — one per task` is the last section; its only `###` headings are `### A1 — <title> (be-documenter, docs)`, `### A2 — …` and `### K1 — …`; each heading is followed by one blank line and a fenced block whose first line is `Depends on: none` or ids of this plan and whose second line is `Agent: be-documenter · Stack: docs`

Each prompt block has a reading order that names the area's primary evidence by fixture path, a line saying the survey is done and must not be redone, two to four traps, its gate command, a commit message, and ends with the close-out line
The plan contains no TBD or TODO and no grouping layer over the tasks (no phases, slices, stages or milestones)
docs/agent-context/be-documenter.md exists and records the area map, the surface counts and the parked list
